name: Paramedian Facial Cleft

criteria.description: Presence of a cleft extending through the midline of the upper lip and nose
Hypoplasia or clefting of nasal structures including nasal bones and cartilage
Abnormalities of the medial canthus or orbital rim including hypertelorism
Presence of additional craniofacial malformations such as cleft palate or midline brain anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of midline facial cleft involving upper lip and nasal structures with or without orbital involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging to assess extent of bony and soft tissue involvement.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Midline cleft of the upper lip extending into the nose
searchTerms: split upper lip reaching the nose
cleft lip extending into nose area

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hypoplasia or clefting of nasal bones and cartilage

searchTerms: eyes spaced farther apart than usual

common.symptomName: Nasal airway obstruction due to structural abnormalities

searchTerms: missing or thin soft tissue in center of face

occasional.symptomName: Epiphora due to lacrimal duct anomalies
searchTerms: excessive tearing from blocked tear ducts
watery eyes due to tear drainage problems
tear overflow from lacrimal duct issues

occasional.symptomName: Feeding difficulties in infancy related to orofacial clefts
searchTerms: trouble feeding as baby due to mouth clefts
difficulty sucking or swallowing in infancy
feeding problems from lip or palate splits

occasional.symptomName: Midline brain anomalies such as agenesis of the corpus callosum
Speech articulation difficulties secondary to cleft palate
searchTerms: difficulty pronouncing words due to cleft palate
articulation issues related to mouth structure

rare.symptomName: Seizures associated with underlying brain malformations
searchTerms: epileptic episodes linked to brain defects

rare.symptomName: Midline endocrine abnormalities such as hypopituitarism
Recurrent respiratory infections due to airway anomalies
searchTerms: frequent lung infections from airway problems
breathing infections due to airway defects

imaging: CT or MRI showing midline facial bone clefts and nasal structure hypoplasia
MRI brain to evaluate for associated midline brain anomalies
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; sporadic cases predominate
Possible association with chromosomal abnormalities in some syndromic cases
other: Clinical photographic documentation of facial cleft
Multidisciplinary evaluation including craniofacial and neurological assessment

distinguishingFeatures: More extensive midline facial clefting including lower lip and mandible
Associated with holoprosencephaly in severe cases
Broad nasal root and hypertelorism without true clefting of the lip
Presence of frontal bossing and median facial skin tags

redFlags: Severe airway obstruction due to nasal and midface anomalies
Associated brain malformations causing neurological deficits
Feeding difficulties leading to failure to thrive
references: Tessier P. Anatomical classification of facial clefts. J Maxillofac Surg. 1976.
Craniofacial Anomalies: Diagnosis and Management, 3rd Edition, 2020
